subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does a plant droop (wilt) if it gets no water for a few days?
prompt_hi: Agar paudhe ko kuch din paani na mile, toh woh murjha kyon jaata hai?
answer: Water keeps the stem and leaves firm and is needed to make food. Without water coming up from the roots, the leaves lose more water than they get, go soft and droop.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Farmers add manure to the soil. So does a plant eat soil and manure as its food? Explain.
prompt_hi: Kisaan mitti mein khaad daalte hain. Toh kya paudha mitti aur khaad ko apna khaana bana ke khaata hai? Samjhao.
answer: No. A plant makes its own food in its leaves using sunlight, water and air. Its roots take water and small amounts of minerals from the soil and manure, which keep it healthy, but soil is not its food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a camel in the Thar desert with a buffalo near a village pond. How does each manage its water?
prompt_hi: Thar registan ke oont aur gaon ke taalab ke paas wali bhains ki tulna karo. Dono apne paani ka intezaam kaise karte hain?
answer: The buffalo drinks often and lies in the pond to stay cool. The camel can go many days without drinking because its body loses very little water, and it drinks a lot at once when it finds water. Its hump stores fat, not water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: On a hot summer day you play cricket for two hours. What happens to the water in your body, and what should you do?
prompt_hi: Garmi ke din tum do ghante cricket khelte ho. Tumhare shareer ke paani ka kya hota hai, aur tumhe kya karna chahiye?
answer: You lose a lot of water as sweat and through breathing, so you feel thirsty and tired. Drink water often and rest in the shade.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Many farmers in Rajasthan use drip irrigation: thin pipes drip water right at the base of each plant. Why is this smarter than flooding the whole field with water?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai kisaan drip irrigation use karte hain: patli pipe se paani boond-boond har paudhe ki jad ke paas girta hai. Ye poore khet mein paani bhar dene se zyada samajhdaari kyon hai?
answer: The water goes straight to the roots, where the plant takes it in, so less water is lost to evaporation or to soil where there are no roots. It saves scarce water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw a plant and use arrows to show the path water takes from the soil to the air. Label each part the water passes.
prompt_hi: Ek paudha banao aur teer (arrows) se dikhao ki paani mitti se hawa tak kaunsa raasta leta hai. Har hissa label karo jahaan se paani guzarta hai.
answer: Soil, then roots, then stem, then leaves, then out as water vapour through tiny openings into the air.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Rohan says: 'A camel's hump is its water tank. That's why it can live in the desert.' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Rohan kehta hai: 'Oont ka kubad uski paani ki tanki hai. Isiliye woh registan mein reh paata hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: The hump stores fat, not water. Camels survive because their bodies lose water very slowly and they can drink a lot at once when they find water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your friend's younger sister waters only the leaves of her plant and thinks plants eat mud. Explain to her how a plant really gets its water and its food.
prompt_hi: Tumhare dost ki chhoti behen apne paudhe ki sirf pattiyon pe paani daalti hai aur sochti hai ki paudhe mitti khaate hain. Use samjhao ki paudha asal mein paani aur khaana kaise paata hai.
answer: Roots take water from the soil and it travels up the stem to the leaves; the leaves make the plant's food using sunlight, water and air. Soil gives water and minerals but is not the plant's food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: say the path water takes inside a plant, from the bottom to the top.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: paudhe ke andar paani neeche se upar kaunsa raasta leta hai?
answer: Roots, then stem, then leaves.

subject: evs
prompt_en: What do we call a smaller river that joins a bigger river?
prompt_hi: Jo chhoti nadi kisi badi nadi mein aakar milti hai, use kya kehte hain?
answer: A tributary.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Outdoors, make a small hill of sand or soil in a tray or on the ground and slowly pour a mug of water on its top. Predict: which way will the water go, and what will it carry with it?
prompt_hi: Bahar ek tray mein ya zameen pe ret ya mitti ka chhota pahad banao, aur uski choti pe dheere-dheere ek mug paani daalo. Guess karo: paani kis taraf jayega, aur apne saath kya le jayega?
answer: The water runs down the slopes from the top to the bottom, making little channels, and carries some sand or soil down with it, which collects at the bottom.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A river rushes down a steep mountain and then reaches flat plains. Predict: in the plains, will it flow faster or slower, and what will happen to the mud it is carrying?
prompt_hi: Ek nadi oonche pahad se tezi se neeche aati hai aur phir samatal maidaan mein pahunchti hai. Guess karo: maidaan mein woh tez bahegi ya dheere, aur jo mitti woh saath laa rahi hai uska kya hoga?
answer: Slower. As it slows down, it drops the fine mud and sand (silt) it was carrying, which makes the land in the plains fertile.

subject: evs
prompt_en: The Narmada starts at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and ends in the Arabian Sea in Gujarat. Using what you know about where the Arabian Sea is, predict: does it flow towards the east or the west? Then check on a map.
prompt_hi: Narmada Madhya Pradesh ke Amarkantak se shuru hoti hai aur Gujarat mein Arabian Sea mein milti hai. Arabian Sea kahaan hai, ye yaad karke guess karo: woh east ki taraf behti hai ya west ki taraf? Phir map pe check karo.
answer: Towards the west, because the Arabian Sea is on India's west side and the river flows from higher land down to that sea.

subject: evs
prompt_en: The Ganga flows into the sea every day. Why does it not run out of water?
prompt_hi: Ganga roz samudra mein behti hai. Phir uska paani khatam kyon nahi hota?
answer: Rain and melting snow and glacier ice in the Himalayas keep feeding it, and tributaries add more. Water from the sea evaporates and comes back as rain, so it is a cycle.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why have so many big towns and cities, like Varanasi, Patna and Rajahmundry, grown up on river banks?
prompt_hi: Varanasi, Patna aur Rajahmundry jaise kai bade shehar nadi ke kinaare hi kyon base hain?
answer: Rivers give water for drinking and farming, fertile soil, fish, and a way to travel and trade.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a river high in the mountains with the same river near the sea. Think about its speed, its width and the land around it.
prompt_hi: Pahadon mein behti nadi aur samudra ke paas wahi nadi, dono ki tulna karo. Uski raftaar, chaudai aur aas-paas ki zameen ke baare mein socho.
answer: In the mountains it is narrow, fast and rocky and cuts deep valleys. Near the sea it is wide and slow, flows over flat land, drops silt and may split into many channels (a delta).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Is there a river, nala or stream near your town? Ask an elder where it begins and where it ends. Is the start higher or lower than the end?
prompt_hi: Tumhare shehar ke paas koi nadi, naala ya dhaara hai? Kisi bade se poochho ki woh kahaan se shuru hoti hai aur kahaan khatam. Shuru wali jagah oonchi hai ya khatam wali?
answer: The start is always higher than the end: it begins at a higher place such as hills, a spring or a lake, and ends in a lower place such as a bigger river, a lake or the sea.

subject: evs
prompt_en: After heavy rain, water flows along the road outside your school and into a drain. How is this like a river's journey?
prompt_hi: Tez baarish ke baad school ke bahar sadak pe paani behta hai aur naali mein chala jaata hai. Ye kisi nadi ke safar jaisa kaise hai?
answer: The water flows downhill from higher to lower places; small streams join into bigger ones like tributaries; it carries mud and leaves; and it ends in a bigger drain or river, like a river reaching the sea.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw a river's journey from a mountain to the sea. Label the source, a tributary, the plains with farms, and the mouth where it meets the sea.
prompt_hi: Pahad se samudra tak ek nadi ka safar banao. Label karo: source (udgam), ek tributary, kheton wale maidaan, aur mouth jahaan woh samudra se milti hai.
answer: Source at the top of the mountains; a tributary joining on the way; plains with farms and towns where the river is wide and slow; the mouth or delta at the sea; arrows pointing downhill towards the sea.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'The sea is full of water, so it fills the rivers. Rivers start at the sea and flow up to the mountains.' Spot the mistake.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Samudra paani se bhara hai, isliye wahi nadiyon ko bharta hai. Nadiyaan samudra se shuru hokar pahadon tak jaati hain.' Galti pakdo.
answer: Water flows downhill, not uphill. Rivers start high in the hills or mountains and flow down into the sea; also, river water is fresh while sea water is salty.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a friend from another country the journey of the Godavari: where it starts, which way it goes, and where it ends.
prompt_hi: Kisi doosre desh ke dost ko Godavari ka safar samjhao: kahaan se shuru hoti hai, kis taraf jaati hai, aur kahaan khatam hoti hai.
answer: It starts in the hills near Trimbakeshwar in Nashik, Maharashtra; flows east across Maharashtra, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, joined by tributaries; slows down in the plains; and ends in the Bay of Bengal.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: does a river flow from high land to low land, or from low land to high land?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: nadi oonchi zameen se neechi zameen ki taraf behti hai, ya neechi se oonchi ki taraf?
answer: From high land to low land, downhill.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name three things that make river water dirty.
prompt_hi: 3 cheezein batao jo nadi ke paani ko ganda karti hain.
answer: Any three: sewage or dirty drain water, factory waste, garbage and plastic, soap from washing clothes or animals, idols made of plaster of Paris with paint.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Find a small slope in a park or garden with one grassy patch and one bare patch of soil. Pour one mug of water at the top of each. Predict: which patch will send down more muddy water, and faster?
prompt_hi: Park ya bageeche mein ek chhoti dhalaan dhoondho jahaan ek jagah ghaas ho aur ek jagah khaali mitti. Dono ke upar ek-ek mug paani daalo. Guess karo: kahaan se zyada aur jaldi matmaila paani neeche aayega?
answer: The bare patch: water runs off quickly and carries mud. On the grassy patch, roots hold the soil and more water soaks in, so less muddy water comes down, and more slowly.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bury a banana peel and a plastic wrapper in a pot of damp soil. After three weeks, dig them up with a stick or spoon (and wash your hands after). Predict what each will look like.
prompt_hi: Geeli mitti wale gamle mein ek kele ka chhilka aur ek plastic ka wrapper daba do. Teen hafte baad lakdi ya chammach se nikaalo (aur baad mein haath dhona). Guess karo dono kaise dikhenge.
answer: The banana peel will be soft, dark and partly broken down by tiny living things (microbes); the plastic wrapper will look almost the same, because plastic does not rot.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put a lump of unbaked mitti (clay) and a small plastic toy in two buckets of water for two days. Predict: which one will soften and mix back into mud, and which one will stay as it is?
prompt_hi: Kachchi mitti ka ek dhela aur ek chhota plastic ka khilona do alag baaltiyon ke paani mein do din ke liye rakh do. Guess karo: kaun naram hokar mitti mein ghul jayega, aur kaun waisa hi rahega?
answer: The clay softens, crumbles and settles as mud, going back to nature; the plastic toy stays the same. This is why towns ask for idols made of natural clay.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do hills that have lost their forests get floods and landslides more often in the monsoon?
prompt_hi: Jin pahadon ke jungle kat gaye hain, wahaan monsoon mein baadh aur landslide zyada kyon hote hain?
answer: Without tree roots to hold the soil and leaves to slow the rain, water rushes down quickly carrying soil, so rivers fill up fast and slopes slide.

subject: evs
prompt_en: During heavy rain, muddy water is flowing fast across the road on your way home. What is the safe thing to do?
prompt_hi: Tez baarish mein ghar jaate waqt sadak pe matmaila paani tezi se beh raha hai. Sabse surakshit kya karna chahiye?
answer: Do not walk or wade into the flowing water; wait at a safe, higher place, tell or call an adult, and follow official warnings. Fast water can knock you over and hide open drains.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare two families after a festival: Family A throws its flowers and plastic bags into the river; Family B puts the flowers in a compost pit and the plastic in the dry-waste bin. What happens to the river in each case?
prompt_hi: Tyohaar ke baad do families ki tulna karo: Family A apne phool aur plastic ki thailiyaan nadi mein phenk deti hai; Family B phoolon ko compost pit mein aur plastic ko sukhe kachre ke dibbe mein daalti hai. Dono baar nadi ka kya hota hai?
answer: With Family A, the plastic stays in the river and harms fish and animals, and large heaps of rotting flowers dirty the water. With Family B, the flowers become manure, the plastic can be recycled, and the river stays cleaner.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your colony is celebrating a festival in which idols are immersed. Suggest two ways to do it without harming the nearby lake.
prompt_hi: Tumhari colony mein ek tyohaar mein murtiyon ka visarjan hota hai. Paas ki jheel ko nuksaan pahunchaye bina ye karne ke do tareeke batao.
answer: Any two: use idols made of natural clay without harmful paints; immerse them in an artificial tank or a bucket at home; remove decorations, plastic and cloth before immersion.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A town is built on low land right next to a river, and it floods every few years. If you were planning a new school there, what would you choose, and why?
prompt_hi: Ek shehar nadi ke bilkul paas neechi zameen pe basa hai aur har kuch saal mein wahaan baadh aati hai. Agar tumhe wahaan naya school banana ho, toh kya chunoge, aur kyon?
answer: Build it on higher ground away from the river's flood land, raise the floor, keep drains clear and plant trees around it, so flood water does not reach the classrooms.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw a river passing a village, a factory and a town. Mark with arrows where dirt could enter the river, and draw one fix next to each place.
prompt_hi: Ek nadi banao jo ek gaon, ek factory aur ek shehar ke paas se guzarti hai. Teer se dikhao ki ganda kahaan se nadi mein ja sakta hai, aur har jagah ke paas ek ilaaj banao.
answer: Village: washing and garbage, fixed with dustbins and compost; factory: waste pipe, fixed by cleaning the waste before it is released; town: sewage drain, fixed with a sewage treatment plant, and plastic, fixed with bins and recycling.

subject: evs
prompt_en: On a picnic, Chintu sees a stream and says, 'This water is so clear, it must be safe to drink!' What's wrong?
prompt_hi: Picnic pe Chintu ek dhaara dekh ke kehta hai, 'Ye paani kitna saaf hai, ise toh seedha pee sakte hain!' Galti kya hai?
answer: Clear water can still have germs and harmful dissolved things we cannot see. Drink only water that is known to be safe, such as water your family has boiled or filtered.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child why cutting trees on hills can bring floods to towns far below.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki pahadon pe ped kaatne se door neeche ke shehron mein baadh kyon aa sakti hai.
answer: Tree roots hold the soil and help rain soak in. Without trees, rain rushes down fast with mud, rivers fill up and overflow downstream in the towns.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name one way your family can help keep a river or lake clean.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek tareeka batao jisse tumhari family kisi nadi ya jheel ko saaf rakhne mein madad kar sakti hai.
answer: Any one: no garbage or plastic in the water, clay idols or immersion tanks, composting festival flowers, not washing with soap in the river, using dustbins.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name three signs that tell you food has spoiled, without tasting it.
prompt_hi: Bina chakhe, 3 nishaaniyaan batao jinse pata chale ki khaana kharaab ho gaya hai.
answer: Any three: a bad or sour smell, slime, a change of colour, fuzzy mould spots, froth or bubbles.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put a slice of bread into each of two zip bags. Sprinkle a few drops of water on one slice and leave the other dry. Seal both and keep them in a warm place for five days. Predict: which gets mould first? (Keep the bags sealed and throw them away sealed at the end.)
prompt_hi: Do zip wali thailiyon mein ek-ek bread slice rakho. Ek slice pe paani ki kuch boondein chhidko, doosri sukhi rehne do. Dono band karke paanch din garam jagah rakho. Guess karo: kis pe pehle phaphoond lagegi? (Thailiyaan band hi rakhna, aur aakhir mein band hi phenk dena.)
answer: The damp slice, because microbes such as mould grow faster where there is moisture and warmth.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your family sets curd every evening. Predict: will it set faster on a hot May night or on a cold January night?
prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar mein roz shaam ko dahi jamaya jaata hai. Guess karo: garam May ki raat mein dahi jaldi jamega ya thandi January ki raat mein?
answer: On the hot May night. The helpful bacteria that turn milk into curd grow and work faster in warmth; in the cold they work slowly, so curd takes longer.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Imagine the same cooked dal left out on the kitchen counter, once on a hot summer afternoon and once on a cool winter day. Predict which one will smell sour first.
prompt_hi: Socho, wahi pakki hui daal kitchen ke counter pe chhod di gayi: ek baar garmi ki dopahar mein, ek baar thandi sardi ke din. Guess karo kaunsi daal pehle khatti badboo degi.
answer: The summer one; microbes grow much faster in warmth, so the dal spoils sooner, even though both are the same age.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why does adding one spoon of old curd to lukewarm milk turn the whole bowl into curd overnight?
prompt_hi: Halke garam doodh mein ek chammach purana dahi daalne se poora katora raat bhar mein dahi kyon ban jaata hai?
answer: The spoon of curd contains helpful bacteria. In the warm milk they multiply and change the milk into curd.
